1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 5..strategy: The main line: it threatens h5, which would trap the bishop, because every square it could go to is covered and the h7 pawn blocks its retreat. Black has to make room at once, and White gains kingside space and the initiative, though the advanced pawn can become a target in the endgame.
1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 5..name: Caro–Kann Defence: Classical Variation, Main Line

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 5..strategy: Heads for f4 to challenge the bishop on g6; from there the knight would also eye d5 and e6, and an exchange would give White the bishop pair. Until it arrives the knight stands on the rim, which gives Black time to organise the centre.
1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 5..name: Caro–Kann Defence: Classical Variation, Flohr Variation

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 5..strategy: Threatens f5 to trap the bishop in the same way as the h-pawn does, but at a higher price: the pawn leaves f2, so e3 loses its guard and White's own kingside is thinner. Black parries the threat with a sound developing move and has no reason to worry.
1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 5..name: Caro–Kann Defence: Classical Variation, Maróczy Attack

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 5..strategy: Gives the bishop the h7 square before h5 can trap it, and takes g5 away from White's pieces. Black accepts that White gains space on the wing and keeps the bishop; the advanced h-pawn cramps Black's kingside but can also turn into a weakness later.
